## choice of the filtering methods and parameters

In this folder, we present analyses aimed at determining the optimal way to filter our datasets. For both A. pisum and A. fabae, we removed all replicates for which no adults remained on the plant. We also applied the interquartile range method to remove outliers. We then selected a minimum number of replicates per genotype—4 for A. fabae and 6 for A. pisum—based on the overall number of genotypes, total number of data points, RMSE, and heritability.

In the subsequent analysis, we decided to conduct GWAS using datasets filtered with minimum replicate numbers of 4, 5, and 6 to assess how this parameter influences the GWAS results. However, only the dataset filtered with a minimum of 4 replicates per genotype for A. fabae and 6 for A. pisum will be retained. The difference between the two datasets can be explained by the initially smaller number of genotypes and the higher rate of genotype loss during filtering in A. fabae dataset.
